1:1.t: "The elder": the writer, traditionally the apostle John. "The lady chosen by God": a woman and her family, or a figure for a church and its members (compare 13).

1:3.t: "Be with you": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "will be with us".

1:8.t: "We": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "you".

1:9.t: "Transgresses": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "runs ahead". "Of Christ" (second time): the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

1:7.t: "Coming in the flesh": the deceivers denied that Jesus truly became human. See 1 John 4:2-3.

1:10.t: "Do not take them into your house": early Christian teachers depended on hospitality. Welcoming false teachers would support their work. John is not forbidding ordinary kindness.
